title: The First Transatlantic Flight
about: who flew it, when, from where to where and how long it took. Include several specific numbers, dates or names where the topic has them, some exact and some rounded or hedged (about, nearly, more than, up to).
passages: On 14 June 1919, two British airmen, pilot John Alcock and NAVIGATOR Arthur Whitten Brown, took off from St. John's in Newfoundland. Their plane was a Vickers Vimy, a large BIPLANE first built as a bomber during the First World War, now fitted with extra fuel tanks. They were trying to win a prize of £10,000 offered by the Daily Mail newspaper for the first nonstop flight across the Atlantic. A few weeks earlier, an American Navy flying boat called the NC-4 had crossed the ocean, but it stopped several times along the way, including in the Azores and Portugal.

The crossing was cold, foggy and frightening. For hours Brown could not see the sun or stars, which he needed to find their position with his SEXTANT, and snow and ice clung to the plane. At one point they dropped dangerously close to the waves. After just under 16 hours and nearly 1,900 miles, they landed on 15 June near Clifden, a small town on the windswept west coast of Ireland. The green field they chose turned out to be a soft BOG, where local families had cut peat to burn for warmth for centuries, so the plane tipped onto its nose. Both men walked away safely, and within days King George V knighted them.
